newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close weaker in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close weaker in thin trading.

text.p: * Main index down 15.61 points (0.49 pct) to 3,186.19
Shares on the Manila Stock Exchange finished lower on Wednesday as investors continued to hold back on fears of a U.S. rate hike, brokers said.

"We were not able to sustain Tuesday's momentum. There is still the U.S. rate hike cloud, everybody's being selective and foreigners cannot move," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
There were 30 gainers and 70 losers while 73 issues were unchanged.
"Sentiment is down as investors are still looking for news to perk up the market," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities & Securities Corp.
Traders said news that the House of Representatives was backing specific tax, instead of ad valorem tax, on beer and cigarettes may not move the market much on Thursday.
